data:
This course will introduce the students to the wide array of
 possibilities and opportunities offered by the arts as a discipline
 beyond practice. The field of art writing and criticism is
 undergoing interesting experimentation in recent times with
 several critics and writers taking recourse to new creative forms
 in writing on art. Similarly, the arts are sustained by an interlinked
 scaffolding of supporters and allies, as can be seen in arts
 management, grant making, conservation, curation, advocacy,
 activism, journalism and scholarship. Practitioners in each of
 these fields, often called mediators or translators of the arts, help
 in the dissemination, perception, transaction, and value-creation
 of arts. In other words, they form the ecosystem within which art
 can thrive. In this course, students will learn how such mediators
 have engaged with the arts through a series of seminars, talks,
 and discussions. Through separate writing workshop modules and
 working groups, students will acquire basic skills in some of these
 practices. The course aims to instill students with a curiosity to
 explore future pathways into the arts, encouraging the use of
 their interdisciplinary skills and knowledge and expanding the
 horizon of the arts beyond professional practice into everyday
 life. This course is best augmented with the Performance
 practicum course offered as well as electives focussed in some of
 these practices.
 Learning Outcomes
 1. Introduction to various practices of mediation and
 engagement with the arts.
 2. Acquiring some basic understanding and working
 knowledge of some of these practices,
 eg. writing, curation, activism etc.
 3. Enabling future interdisciplinary pathways into the arts.
Associate Professor of Practice, Literature and Global Arts
